recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. It is a narrow correction to stale prose in the FHIR-3356 search guidance and does not reopen the later Observation relationship-model decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-3356 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Observation search issue. The initial related-target concern was narrowed in comments after the existing related composite was noted; the approved remaining request was to clarify whether related/relatedTarget search inclusion recurses and how include depth is controlled.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in git-svn revision 4580, imported as commit 13da0d4b9ad91765695173ebcd8b31387120f812 with subject '#5679 and #3356: _revinclude and changes to _include'. That commit rewrote source/search.html include guidance and added server-discretion language for recursive include depth.
additional_context: The current source/search.html page still contains the include-depth clarification and is the active core search narrative. Later Observation work, especially FHIR-10118, replaced the old Observation.related structure and related search vocabulary with explicit elements and search parameters such as Observation.hasMember/has-member and Observation.derivedFrom/derived-from. The examples had already been updated to use Observation:has-member, but one adjacent sentence still named the obsolete related parameter.
reconciliation: Changed source/search.html so the circular Observation _include example asks for _include based on the has-member parameter. The existing non-recursive default, iterate modifier, and server-discretion depth language were left unchanged because they already satisfy the FHIR-3356 recursion decision.
source_changes: source/search.html: updated the Observation circular _include example prose to cite the current has-member search parameter instead of the obsolete related parameter.

related_jiras.note: Published Observation change replacing Observation.related with explicit relationship elements; used as context for why the current search prose must use has-member.
